messages:
irene_support: heads up — AcmeCorp just escalated, their support ticket shows p99 for /v1/generate spiking to ~3.2s for the past 30m. They say their users see timeouts. ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-8921

ops-bot: ALERT: alert=p99_latency_high service=api-route:/v1/generate value=3200ms window=30m

sam_obs: I pulled dashboards. Our internal p99 panel (histogram-rollup) shows a much smaller increase — ~1.1s. Can you paste the customer metrics or repro?

devon_sre: I ran a quick raw histogram query from prod events; I'm seeing a tail at ~3s but only for requests with header X-Client: acme-internal. Suspect their traffic shape is different. Query used: ```sql
SELECT bucket, count FROM request_latency_histogram WHERE route='/v1/generate' AND ts > now() - interval '1 hour' AND client='acme'```

irene_support: customer provided a snippet from their front-end synthetic probe (browser): ```json
{"url": "/v1/generate","latency_ms": 3234,"ts":"2026-02-18T21:10:12Z","region":"eu-west-1"}
```

maria_platform: two immediate suspects: client-side vs server-side measurement (dns/connect/blocking) and aggregation window / histogram bucket boundaries. The support probe measures end-to-end which includes CDN + network. Our p99 panel is service-side.

aj_prod: Also check our edge/proxy logs. We had a config push 20m ago to change NGINX keepalive timeout on the edge pool in eu-west-1. Could be causing extra handshakes for certain long-lived clients. I'm tailing the proxy logs now.

devon_sre: re: metrics math — Sam, which panels are you comparing? The customer screenshot is from their real users; are we mixing synthetic and server histograms? Our dashboard uses rollups that sample every 15s and bucketize into power-of-two boundaries. That can hide a small subpopulation.

sam_obs: I'm looking at dashboard: Metrics > service.latency.p99 (rollup) and Histogram > request_latency_histo.rollup. The rollup aggregator computes p99 by merging quantile summaries from 1m buckets. If a tiny spike of high latency lasts <1s per minute, the rollup can undercount.

irene_support: customer insists it's visible in their SLO graphs — they show consistent p95->p99 divergence only for their API key. They provided example request ids: req_9a4f, req_9a5b.

devon_sre: grabbing traces for req_9a4f: ```
TRACE req_9a4f
- client_connect 120ms
- tls_handshake 310ms
- proxy_queue 45ms
- upstream_processing 2450ms
- response_write 65ms
TOTAL 2990ms
```

sam_obs: upstream_processing 2450ms — that's our service time. That should be visible in our histograms. Why is the p99 panel not showing it? Two hypotheses: (1) the ingestion pipeline filters out requests with header X-Client:acme in the rollup stream (legacy filter), (2) different metric tags used for rollup p99 vs raw histograms.

maria_platform: I searched the ingestion configs — there is a legacy sampling rule that drops high-cardinality client tags from the quantile rollup stream to save memory. It looks like client=acme is being dropped for rollups but preserved in raw histograms. That would explain the discrepancy.

aj_prod: If that's true, then the rollup p99 will be computed from a dataset that excludes Acme traffic — i.e., an undercount. We need a mitigation: temporarily disable that sampling rule for the affected customers and trigger a re-rollup for the last 1 hour.

irene_support: customer needs a short-term workaround while we fix metrics — suggested support reply: "we recommend adding a retry/backoff client-side and we will investigate server-side config and provide an ETA." They want ETA asap.

devon_sre: mitigation plan: 1) enable full tag retention for client key 'acme' in the rollup stream (hotfix) 2) kick a backfill job to recompute the 1h rollup for /v1/generate 3) monitor p99 for that client specifically 4) while backfill runs, surface raw histogram panel to customer-facing dashboard.

sam_obs: I'll implement (1) and kick (2). For the backfill I'll run: ```bash
# backfill rollups for last 1h for client=acme and route=/v1/generate
python infra/tools/recompute_rollups.py --from $(date -u -d '1 hour ago' +%s) --to $(date -u +%s) --tags client=acme,route=/v1/generate
```

maria_platform: ops check — making that sampling rule change will increase memory pressure on the rollup service. We should only whitelist specific customer tags and set a TTL. I'll add a temporary config: client_whitelist={'acme': 3600} and deploy to rollup-ingest.

aj_prod: deployed nginx rollback earlier, edge config is stable. I'll tail for any increase in connection churn. So far nothing alarming.

ops-bot: DEPLOYMENT: rollup-ingest@v3.14 deployed by sam_obs — config change: client_whitelist add acme ttl=3600

sam_obs: kicked the recompute job — ETA ~7min for 1h window. Posting live query against raw histogram to compare: ```promql
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_latency_bucket{route="/v1/generate",client="acme"}[5m])) by (le))
```

devon_sre: traced a few more sample requests — pattern seems tied to a specific model shard in eu-west-1 that occasionally has long GC pauses when queue depth is high. I've raised a ticket with inference-runtime: INF-456 to investigate shard health and adjust prefetch/batching.

sam_obs: recompute finished. New rollup p99 for client=acme now shows ~2.95s for the window — aligns with customer probes. I'm updating the customer and linking the new dashboard.

irene_support: responding to customer: "we've identified the root cause of the discrepancy: our rollup sampling excluded your client tag which hid the tail. We've recomputed rollups and your p99 shows the elevated latency. We're investigating the runtime GC spikes and will propose a mitigation shortly. Temporary recommendation: add client-side retry/backoff."

maria_platform: follow-up action items: - Create config PR to make whitelist behavior explicit and add alert for rollup-tag-drop events - Add an ingestion test to catch future silent drops - Document how rollup sampling affects quantile panels

aj_prod: created infra ticket INFRA-980 to add an alert on rollup memory pressure + tag drop rate.

support-bot: TICKET UPDATE: INC-8921 AcmeCorp updated — assigned to devon_sre, customer notified.

devon_sre: thanks all. Closing loop here: root cause = rollup sampling rule + intermittent GC on inference shard. Short-term fix = rollup whitelist + backfill. Long-term = runtime GC tuning and better ingestion tests. I'll own the runtime ticket.

irene_support: customer replied: "thanks, seeing improvement and appreciate the quick turnaround." :thumbsup:

sam_obs: note for postmortem: be explicit on docs that "dashboard p99" may differ from "end-to-end user p99" when rollups or tag sampling are in effect.

maria_platform: filing a brief postmortem doc after runtime fixes are deployed.

aj_prod: if anyone wants traces or raw logs for the sample req ids, ping me and I'll hand them over.

irene_support: closing thread for now, will reopen if customer reports regression. Thanks team :)
